ops.text: Liability Cap. Except for Excluded Claims, each party's aggregate liability under this Agreement will not exceed the greater of (a) fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000. "Excluded Claims" means a party's breach of its confidentiality, data protection or security obligations, its indemnification obligations, its gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud, and its infringement of the other party's intellectual property rights. Customer's payment obligations, being all amounts due from PB under this Agreement, are not damages for purposes of this cap.

proposal.summary: Insert a mutual liability cap with uncapped Excluded Claims after § 15.11

quote: 15.11 Limitation of Liability. TO THE MAXIMUM EXTENT PERMITTED BY LAW AND NOTWITHSTANDING ANY PROVISION IN THIS AGREEMENT TO THE CONTRARY, NEITHER PARTY WILL BE LIABLE TO THE OTHER PARTY FOR ANY INDIRECT, INCIDENTAL, CONSEQUENTIAL, SPECIAL, RELIANCE OR PUNITIVE DAMAGES OR LOST OR IMPUTED PROFITS OR ROYALTIES OR COST OF PROCUREMENT OF SUBSTITUTE GOODS OR SERVICES
rationale: Section 15.11 is the only limitation-of-liability provision (the arbitration clause at § 15.10.2.4 merely repeats the consequential/punitive damages waiver). It is mutual as to indirect/consequential damages, but there is no aggregate monetary cap anywhere in the Agreement, so each party's direct liability is unlimited — a failure of the fallback, which requires a mutual cap with carve-outs. We therefore insert a concise mutual cap at the greater of fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000, with uncapped Excluded Claims (confidentiality, data protection and security, indemnification, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, IP infringement) and an express statement that Customer's payment obligations are not damages for cap purposes, which preserves PB's Article 6 / Section 14.2 payment position. The existing exclusion-of-damages sentences are left untouched, and indemnities are not double-flagged — they are only referenced as sitting outside the cap.

quote: 3.19 Exclusivity Commitment of SFJ. During the applicable Exclusive Period, SFJ shall not, and shall cause its Affiliates not to, either by itself or through a Third Party, conduct human clinical trials of, or sell, offer for sale or have sold:
rationale: The Agreement imposes no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation on us, so it meets the preferred position. The only exclusivity covenant (§ 3.19, p0369–p0374) runs against SFJ during the Exclusive Period and therefore benefits us — under the rule this is expressly acceptable and not flagged. The § 2.4 Approved CRO / Approved Vendor architecture (p0262–p0264) applies reciprocally to each Party and lets us contract with any listed or JDC-approved provider; it is a joint-governance quality gate, not a requirements or single-source commitment, and does not channel our sourcing to SFJ. § 3.14.2.1 (p0359) restricts SFJ to using Product supplied by us, and § 3.14.1.1 (p0355) confirms we manufacture directly or through an Approved Vendor of our choosing — again in our favour. Restrictions in § 7.5 (e.g. the Licensing Transaction consent at p0552) limit out-licensing and financing rather than our freedom to buy from other suppliers, and are addressed under the financing/restrictive-covenant rules rather than this one. No redline required.

quote: In consideration of the Approval Payments to be made under this Agreement (if and to the extent applicable), and in further consideration of the payment by PB to SFJ of [***], SFJ shall sell and transfer to PB, and PB shall acquire from SFJ, the sole and exclusive ownership, even as to SFJ, of the Trial Data Package including all Research Results as set forth below in this Section 11.1.1.4.
rationale: This is a clinical development funding agreement, not a supply/licence deal, and there is no counterparty-to-customer licence grant anywhere in it (searches for grant language return only PB's security-interest grant to SFJ at p0537). The rule's protective purpose is satisfied on better-than-preferred terms: PB retains sole and exclusive ownership of all Existing PB Intellectual Property and of all Trial Inventions regardless of inventorship (p0650, p0651, p0659), SFJ and its Affiliates and Permitted Third Parties assign Trial Inventions to PB, and SFJ's interim ownership of the Trial Data Package is converted into PB's "sole and exclusive ownership, even as to SFJ" (p0663), with Research Results treated at all times as PB's Confidential Information (PB as disclosing Party) pre-transfer. Ownership is perpetual and irrevocable by definition, needs no affiliate/contractor extension, and passes with a permitted assignment to a successor (Section 15.6, referenced in the Licensing Transaction definition at p0146). The only grants running the other way (security interest, sublicensing constraints in p0084/p0146, Permitted Lien carve-out at p0598) restrict us rather than licence us and are the subject of other rules, so no redline here. Note for the file: the agreement contains no express interim licence for PB to use the Trial Data Package before the purchase closes; PB's disclosing-Party status over Research Results and its regulatory access rights make this a drafting nicety rather than a material gap.

rationale: The agreement imposes no non-compete or field-of-use restriction on PB, so it meets the preferred position (no restriction on Customer). The only exclusivity/competing-product covenant is § 3.19 (p0369–p0374), which runs one way against SFJ and its Affiliates during the Exclusive Period (p0085), and therefore benefits us — per the rule's detection guidance, restrictions binding the counterparty are acceptable and are not flagged. The "Competing Product" and "Brilinta Competing Product" definitions (p0057, p0029) are used only in SFJ's covenant; there is no reciprocal restraint on PB. Searches for "shall not develop/engage in", "field of use", "compete" and "exclusivity" returned no PB-side restraint. The PB-side negative covenants in § 7.5 (p0545–p0557) are financing/collateral covenants (indebtedness, liens on PB Intellectual Property, distributions and Prohibited Investments, sales of royalty streams, further negative pledges) and do not limit the businesses PB may operate or the products PB may buy or build. Noted but not flagged here: § 7.5.5 (p0552) gives SFJ a consent right over non-Excluded Licensing Transactions, which constrains our licensing freedom; it is a collateral-protection term tied to the funded Product rather than a competing-product or field-of-use restraint, it carries an Excluded Licensing Transaction carve-out and an expedited arbitration challenge (p0553–p0554), and it belongs to a separate commercial term that should not be double-flagged under this rule. quote: 9.1 Accounting. Each Party will maintain materially complete and accurate accounting records related to this Agreement in accordance with GAAP.
rationale: The Agreement grants SFJ no audit, inspection or verification right over PB, its records, premises or systems. Article 9 (p0624–p0625) imposes only mutual record-keeping/retention obligations (GAAP accounting records; Development books and records "in sufficient detail to verify compliance"), with no accompanying access or examination right. § 3.6 (p0321–p0322) is a mutual quality-oversight regime in which each Party audits its own Permitted Third Parties (and PB audits the Product manufacturing facilities) and shares the resulting reports — SFJ audits PB's vendors' facilities, not PB. § 3.5.5 (p0318) and § 5.4.4.3 (p0453) are report-sharing and regulatory-inspection notification provisions, and § 3.18.2 (p0367) is financial-statement reporting; none confers audit or system-access rights. There is therefore no frequency, notice, cost or system-access term to constrain: the position is better than preferred (zero audit exposure for us), so no redline is warranted. We note for the record that the "sufficient detail to verify compliance" language in § 9.2 should not later be argued into an implied access right; if SFJ seeks an express audit right in negotiation, we would apply the preferred limits (once per 12 months, 30 days' notice, independent auditor, SFJ's cost, no system access).

That fails both the preferred position (no liquidated damages or penalties payable by Customer) and the fallback (a single early-termination fee capped at 3 months' fees as the sole liquidated amount). Our edit changes only the operative payment words so that no liquidated damages or penalty is payable by PB on that termination, leaving the purchase and exclusive-remedy mechanics intact. The fallback is not met (and need not be, since the locked target is preferred): no early-termination fee, no 3-months'-fees cap, and no sole-liquidated-amount statement. The edit is narrowly scoped to the single payment formula in p0750, so minimality is satisfied. Intent is not preserved: the surviving verb phrase "PB will pay SFJ, within [***] of the date of termination, no liquidated damages or penalty" is internally incoherent — a payment obligation with a payment window but nothing payable — and should be recast as "PB will not be required to pay SFJ any liquidated damages or penalty in respect of Development Costs...". quote: PB shall notify SFJ in writing of the total amount of Development Costs (inclusive of all Development Costs paid or incurred since the Effective Date) that PB elects to have SFJ fund (the "Elected Total Amount"), which shall be no less than $110 million and no more than $120 million.
rationale:
This is a co-development funding agreement in which the payment flow runs toward us: SFJ funds up to $120m of Development Costs (§ 4.1, § 4.2), and our payments to SFJ under ARTICLE 6 are Approval Payments that only become due "following Regulatory Approval" (§ 6.1.1, § 6.1.2). There is no minimum purchase commitment, take-or-pay, shortfall penalty or volume restriction imposed on PB, so the rule sits at the preferred position (fees only for what is actually delivered/contingent milestones).

We reviewed the two nearest analogues flagged in planning and neither functions as a take-or-pay on us: (i) the $110m floor on the Elected Total Amount (§ 4.2.3(ii)) is a floor on how much funding we must accept from SFJ, not on what we must buy, and it is only triggered after a Successful Phase 3 Interim Analysis; and (ii) the excess-cost allocation in § 4.1 / § 4.2.3 (Development Costs above $120m "will be borne by PB", plus the covenant to "spend at least an amount equal to the amount of funding paid by SFJ") is a use-of-proceeds and cost-overrun covenant on our own development programme rather than a purchase obligation to the counterparty. Both are further mitigated by our at-will exit in § 14.2.2, exercisable at any time after SFJ has paid or incurred $60m and before first Regulatory Approval, and by the Buy-Out Payment election in § 6.7. The 300% termination payment under § 14.2.2 is a priced financing return rather than a shortfall penalty and is addressed under the termination/exit-cost rules, not here. No redline proposed.

quote: 15.16 Nonsolicitation. During the Term and for a period of [***] thereafter, neither Party shall solicit an employee of the other Party who is or has been involved in the performance or oversight of any of the development activities hereunder to terminate his or her employment and accept employment or work as a consultant with the soliciting Party. Notwithstanding the foregoing, nothing herein shall restrict or preclude the Parties' right to make generalized searches for employees by way of a general solicitation for employment placed in a trade journal, newspaper or website.
rationale: § 15.16 sits at our fallback position: the non-solicit is fully mutual (binding SFJ equally), is limited to employees who are or have been involved in the performance or oversight of the development activities (not all personnel), prohibits only active solicitation to leave (there is no "no-hire" or "employ or engage" restriction), and carries an express general-advertising carve-out for generalized searches via trade journal, newspaper or website. No other non-solicit or no-hire language appears elsewhere in the document. Two minor sub-elements short of preferred, noted but not flagged: the tail duration is redacted ([***] after the Term) so it cannot be confirmed as 12 months, and there is no separate express carve-out for unsolicited approaches — though the solicitation-only formulation largely achieves that effect. If the redacted tail turns out to exceed 24 months, that would move the clause into walk-away territory and should be revisited.

A full-text search for "renew"/"automatically renew"/"Renewal Term" returns no auto-renewal, evergreen extension, non-renewal notice window or renewal price-uplift mechanic anywhere in the Agreement (the only "renewal" hits relate to IP registrations, Permitted Liens refinancing and insurance coverage). There is therefore no renewal to exit and no notice window to compute; any extension of this development-funding arrangement would require mutual written agreement, which matches the playbook's preferred position. No walk-away features (multi-year auto-renewals or >90-day non-renewal notice) are present. PB also retains at-will termination (§ 14.2.2) and other termination rights, so exit is not constrained by a renewal mechanic. No redline needed.

quote: 14.3.2 effective as of such termination, SFJ shall, and it hereby does, assign to PB all of SFJ's and its Affiliates' right, title and interest in and to all Product Filings then owned or Controlled by SFJ or any of its Affiliates; provided that if any such Product Filing is not immediately transferable in a country, SFJ shall provide PB with all benefit of such Product Filing and such assistance and cooperation as necessary or reasonably requested by PB to timely transfer such Product Filing to PB or its designee
rationale: The agreement already delivers, in our favor, everything this rule targets and more. On any termination, § 14.3 (p0782–p0789) requires SFJ to (i) assign sole and exclusive ownership of the Trial Data Package and Research Results to PB (§ 14.3.1, and § 11.1.1.4 buy-back), (ii) assign all Product Filings and, where a filing is not immediately transferable, give PB the full benefit plus "such assistance and cooperation as necessary or reasonably requested by PB" (§ 14.3.2), (iii) within a set period deliver true, correct and complete copies of all Product Filings and disclose all previously-undisclosed Research Results (§ 14.3.3), (iv) at PB's sole election either wind down the Clinical Trials at SFJ's cost or transfer control to PB and continue conducting them for a stated period to enable transfer without interruption (§ 14.3.4), and (v) assign all CRO, Site and Vendor Agreements and cooperate on transition notices (§ 14.3.5). Deletion/return of our confidential materials is covered by § 10.3, which gives the disclosing party the choice of return or destruction "with such destruction being certified in writing by an authorized officer of the Receiving Party." These provisions are at or above the preferred position: data/records come back to us, transition assistance is available at PB's election (trial continuation at PB's cost, mirroring the "then-current rates" concept), and certified destruction follows. The specific day/month periods are redacted as "[***]" in this copy and the assistance duration is not expressed as a flat six months — we should confirm the redacted periods on the execution copy, but these are timing details rather than material failures, and § 14.4.3 expressly makes Articles 10 and 11 and §§ 14.2–14.3 survive termination. No redline warranted; this is a customer-favorable exit regime.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We added an SFJ indemnity for Third Party claims that SFJ's services or deliverables infringe Intellectual Property, with the usual PB modification, combination and specification exclusions, procure/modify/replace/refund remedies and a 3x annual fees super-cap. Our playbook does not accept IP infringement risk running one way against us.

ops.text: SFJ IP Indemnity. SFJ will indemnify the PB Indemnified Parties from any and all Losses arising or resulting from any Claim by a Third Party alleging that the services or deliverables provided by SFJ under this Agreement infringe or misappropriate such Third Party's Intellectual Property, except to the extent such Claim arises from modifications made by PB, combination of such services or deliverables by PB with items not supplied by SFJ, or SFJ's compliance with specifications provided by PB. SFJ will, at its option, procure for PB the right to continue using the infringing item, modify it or replace it, and if none of the foregoing is available on commercially reasonable terms, refund the amounts paid for it. SFJ's aggregate liability under this Section 12.1.3 will not exceed 3x the annual fees payable under this Agreement.

proposal.summary: Add SFJ third-party IP infringement indemnity with standard exclusions, procure/modify/replace/refund remedies and 3x annual fees super-cap

quote: (f) actual or alleged infringement of any Third Party's Intellectual Property by the Product or by either Party in performing its duties or obligations hereunder with respect to the Product;
rationale: SFJ's indemnity at § 12.1.1 (p0687–p0691) has no third-party IP infringement limb, while our indemnity at § 12.1.2(f) (p0695) covers infringement "by the Product or by either Party in performing its duties or obligations hereunder", so we carry IP risk for SFJ's own performance. That is a one-way Customer IP indemnity and fails the fallback. We target the fallback level: preferred would require rewriting our own § 12.1.2 to strip the Product-supply, breach, Protocol, Subject-injury and Commercialization limbs down to Customer-provided content and breach of law, which cannot pass the minimality gate here. The single fallback insertion adds an SFJ IP indemnity with the usual PB modification, combination and specification exclusions, procure/modify/replace/refund remedies and a 3x annual fees super-cap; notice, control and cooperation procedure already exists at §§ 12.2.1–12.2.5 and is left untouched.

verification.notes: The inserted Section 12.1.3 delivers every atomic element of the fallback: an SFJ IP infringement indemnity for the PB Indemnified Parties, the three usual exclusions (PB modifications, PB combinations, PB specifications), the full procure/modify/replace/refund remedy ladder, and a 3× annual fees super-cap. Minimality is satisfied: no existing sentence was altered, deleted or duplicated; a concise new subsection was added where no Vendor IP indemnity existed, and the numbering (12.1.3) matches the internal cross-reference in the cap. Preferred is not met and was not targeted: no express defence obligation, no breach-of-law or Vendor data-breach heads, and PB's own broad indemnity in 12.1.2 (including the two-way IP infringement head (f)) is left untouched rather than narrowed to PB-provided content and PB's breach of law. Note for the rationale, not a deviation: "annual fees payable under this Agreement" is not a defined concept in this co-development agreement (which speaks in Development Costs), so the quantum of the super-cap may be uncertain; consider tying it to a defined payment metric to avoid an arguably nil cap on our own indemnity.

quote: 12.3.2 Minimum Requirements. Commencing as of the start of the Clinical Trials and thereafter, during the Term (or longer if otherwise stated below), at a minimum, each Party will maintain the following types of insurance coverage at a minimum level that is the greater of (a) the highest minimum level required by Applicable Law in the countries in which the Clinical Trials and other obligations hereunder are being performed or (b) the following (to the extent different).
rationale: An insurance regime is present and substantially exceeds the rule's structural expectations, so no redline is warranted. § 12.3.1–12.3.2 obliges each Party (including SFJ) to carry commercial general liability, umbrella excess liability, clinical trials liability and, for subcontractors providing professional services, professional liability insurance, in each case at the greater of the stated limits or the highest limit required by Applicable Law (which picks up statutory workers' compensation), with insurers rated at least "A-" A.M. Best and policies primary and non-contributing. Certificates of insurance are supplied on written request pre-signing and annually (§ 12.3.1), advance written notice is required on cancellation, non-renewal or material change, and each Party must ensure subcontractors and Permitted Third Parties are insured before continuing work (§ 12.3.2). § 12.3.3 adds additional-insured status for the other Party on clinical trial liability cover, and § 12.3.4 allocates product liability cover with the other Party named as additional insured. § 12.3.2 also confirms insurance does not cap either Party's liability. Two minor sub-elements fall short of the preferred wording and are noted rather than flagged: (i) there is no dedicated cyber/privacy liability line, though this is a clinical development funding arrangement rather than a hosting or data-processing engagement, and clinical trial and professional liability cover carries the relevant risk; and (ii) the numeric limits are redacted ([***]) in our copy, so the USD thresholds cannot be independently verified — we should confirm the unredacted figures against the preferred limits in diligence. The obligations are mutual and largely protective of us, so flagging them would work against our interest.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot accept SFJ holding the Trial Data Package and Research Results with no rights reserved to us pending the purchase, so we have added a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence back (with sublicensing) to use and modify that data for our business, while confirming SFJ owns its generic tools and know-how.

ops.text: SFJ shall own its generic tools and know-how used in performing its obligations hereunder, and SFJ hereby grants to PB a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free license, with the right to sublicense, to use and modify the Trial Data Package and all Research Results for its business, and such license shall survive any expiration or termination of this Agreement.

proposal.summary: Add SFJ generic tools/know-how ownership and a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence back to PB of the Trial Data Package and Research Results

quote: 11.1.1.4 Trial Data Package. SFJ shall be the sole and exclusive owner of the Trial Data Package including the Research Results included therein.
rationale: Ownership of pre-existing PB IP (11.1.1.1) and of Trial Inventions (11.1.1.3, with SFJ assignment) is favourable to us and untouched. The failure is Section 11.1.1.4: SFJ is sole and exclusive owner of the Trial Data Package, which by definition (1.1.193) covers all Information generated in the Clinical Trials by or on behalf of a Party — including the clinical data we and our CROs/Sites generate — and PB only obtains ownership by paying the Approval Payments plus a further redacted sum. No interim licence or use right is reserved to PB anywhere; the Research Results confidentiality deeming (p0062) confers no use rights. That fails both the preferred position and the fallback. Because SFJ's ownership underpins the development-funding and termination payment structure (Sections 6.1, 14.2–14.3), we take the fallback: SFJ owns its generic tools and know-how, and PB receives a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence, sublicensable, to use and modify the Trial Data Package and Research Results for its business, surviving termination.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We removed the $60 million funding gate and the pre-first-approval cut-off so PB as Customer may terminate for convenience at any time on 90 days' notice, and replaced the 300% multiple with an early-termination fee capped at three (3) months' Development Costs. We also limited SFJ's discretionary exits (§§ 14.2.6 and 14.2.10) to the end of the then-current term on 90 days' notice; this is our fallback position on convenience termination.

ops.newText: PB as Customer may terminate this Agreement for convenience at any time upon 90 days' prior written notice to SFJ. In the event that PB terminates this Agreement pursuant to this Section 14.2.2 then in exchange for purchasing the Trial Data Package including the Research Results included therein as set forth in Section 11.1.1.4, PB will pay SFJ, within [***] of the date of termination, an amount not exceeding three (3) months' Development Costs as the sole early-termination fee.
ops.oldText: PB may terminate this Agreement at any time after SFJ has paid or incurred a total of $60 million of Development Costs and prior to the date of receipt of the first Regulatory Approval upon [***] prior written notice to SFJ. In the event that PB terminates this Agreement pursuant to this Section 14.2.2 then in exchange for purchasing the Trial Data Package including the Research Results included therein as set forth in Section 11.1.1.4, PB will pay SFJ, within [***] of the date of termination, an amount equal to three hundred percent (300%) of Development Costs paid or incurred by SFJ prior to such termination.

ops.text: SFJ as Vendor may terminate this Agreement for convenience only effective at the end of the then-current term and only upon 90 days' prior written notice to PB; Sections 14.2.6 and 14.2.10 are limited accordingly.

proposal.summary: Make PB's convenience exit unconditional on 90 days' notice with the exit fee capped at 3 months' Development Costs, and allow SFJ convenience termination only effective at the end of the then-current term on 90 days' notice.

quote: PB may terminate this Agreement at any time after SFJ has paid or incurred a total of $60 million of Development Costs and prior to the date of receipt of the first Regulatory Approval upon [***] prior written notice to SFJ.
rationale: PB's nominal at-will right at § 14.2.2 fails the fallback on material terms: it is unavailable until SFJ has funded $60 million of Development Costs and lapses on the first Regulatory Approval, and exercise triggers 300% of Development Costs, far above a 3-month fee cap. SFJ's discretionary exits at §§ 14.2.6 and 14.2.10 are exercisable "at any time" in its "sole discretion" with no end-of-term limitation and no notice period. We therefore sit the proposal at the fallback: an unconditional PB convenience exit on 90 days' notice, an early-termination fee capped at three (3) months' Development Costs, and SFJ convenience termination only effective at the end of the then-current term on 90 days' notice.

verification.notes: All four fallback atomic elements are met: a Customer convenience right, 90 days' notice (within the 60–90 band), an early-termination fee capped at three months' Development Costs, and a Vendor convenience right confined to end-of-term on 90 days' notice. Preferred fails on two independent elements: notice is 90 rather than 30 days and there is no pro-rata refund of prepaid fees, so the clause sits at the locked fallback level only. Minimality is not fully satisfied: the alias tags "as Customer" and "as Vendor" are unnecessary labelling of already-defined parties, and the trailing sweep "Sections 14.2.6 and 14.2.10 are limited accordingly" reaches beyond convenience termination into the change-of-control and JSC-deadlock exits, which are triggered rights rather than convenience rights. Intent is preserved on balance: the Trial Data Package purchase mechanic, Approval Payment/Buy-Out adjustments and the Section 14.2.6 payment formula remain effective, and the express "limited accordingly" override avoids a bare contradiction, though it leaves the scope of the limitation on §§14.2.6/14.2.10 somewhat imprecise. Note for the rationale rather than as a deviation: removal of the $60 million spend gate and the pre-first-approval cut-off expands Customer's exit and benefits our party, so it should not be flagged.

This is our fallback position and § 13.6.2 already carves out Article 13 warranties from the disclaimer.

ops.text: SFJ Performance Warranty. SFJ warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; (b) for 90 days following delivery, any software provided by SFJ will conform to its documentation; and (c) for 30 days following performance of the Services, the Services will conform to their documentation. PB's remedy for breach of this warranty is repair, replacement or refund of the amounts paid for the non-conforming software or Services.

proposal.summary: Insert an SFJ performance warranty at § 13.5.1: professional and workmanlike Services, 90-day software conformance to documentation, 30-day Services period from performance, with repair, replacement or refund.

quote: 13.5 SFJ Representation, Warranty and Covenant. SFJ hereby represents, warrants and covenants that it will have, as and when needed, sufficient funds to satisfy its obligations hereunder.
rationale: SFJ performs real work under this Agreement (it is sponsor in the SFJ Territory and conducts the Clinical Trials there), but its only warranty is the funding representation in § 13.5, and § 13.6.2 disclaims all warranties except those set out in Article 13. There is therefore no performance warranty and no warranty remedy, which fails the fallback on both elements. We add a short § 13.5.1 supplying only the fallback package — professional and workmanlike Services, 90-day software conformance to documentation, 30-day Services period measured from performance, with repair, replacement or refund — leaving § 13.5 and the mutual outcome disclaimer in § 13.6.1 (which benefits PB) untouched; the Article 13 carve-out in § 13.6.2 preserves the new warranty.

verification.notes: The insertion completes every atomic element of the locked fallback level: professional and workmanlike Services, 90-day software conformance to documentation, 30-day Services conformance measured from performance, and the full repair/replacement/refund remedy set. Preferred level is not met (90 days rather than 12 months for software, 30 rather than 90 days for Services, and no compliance-with-laws or malicious-code warranties), which is consistent with the locked fallback target. Minimality holds: a single concise warranty paragraph was added where no performance warranty existed at all; no preferred-only durations, re-performance remedy, or boilerplate were smuggled in, and no existing sentence was rewritten. Intent is preserved: Section 13.5 funding warranty and the Section 13.6.2 disclaimer remain fully effective, and the disclaimer's 'EXCEPT AS OTHERWISE SET FORTH IN THIS ARTICLE 13' carve-out keeps the new warranty operative. Minor note only (not a deviation): 'Services', 'software' and 'documentation' are not defined terms in this co-development agreement, so they will be read in their ordinary sense; a cross-reference to the relevant work statement would tighten scope.
